steps.title: Conjugation Intro
steps.subtitle: How a Japanese verb changes shape

steps.title: い-adjectives · Negative
steps.subtitle: Adjectives that conjugate on their own
steps.point: Every negative so far ends in ない, and ない is an い-adjective itself. Whatever an い-adjective does, ない does too — which is where the next lesson starts.

steps.title: い-adjectives · Past
steps.subtitle: Adjectives that conjugate on their own

steps.title: Negative past
steps.subtitle: ない is an い-adjective
steps.point: The past of a negative is the い-adjective past of ない: replace its い with かった. 書[か]かない → 書[か]かなかった, exactly as 高[たか]くない → 高[たか]くなかった.

steps.title: て-form
steps.subtitle: The connector half the grammar is built on

steps.title: Adjective て-form
steps.subtitle: And the て-form of ない
steps.point: An い-adjective replaces its い with くて: 高[たか]い → 高[たか]くて. ない is one, so the て-form of a negative is なくて: 書[か]かない → 書[か]かなくて.

steps.title: する, 来[く]る, 行[い]く · Negative
steps.subtitle: The verbs that break the rules

steps.title: する, 来[く]る, 行[い]く · Past
steps.subtitle: The verbs that break the rules

steps.title: する, 来[く]る, 行[い]く · て-form
steps.subtitle: The verbs that break the rules

steps.title: ある and いる
steps.subtitle: To exist — with a negative that comes from nowhere
steps.point: ある's negative is simply ない — the same ない every negative ends in, so its past is なかった and its て-form なくて.

steps.title: Progressive
steps.subtitle: Something happening right now
steps.point: ている is the verb いる after a て-form, and conjugates exactly like it: 食[た]べていない, 食[た]べていた, 食[た]べていなかった.

steps.title: いい
steps.subtitle: The adjective that conjugates as よい

steps.title: な-adjectives · Negative
steps.subtitle: Adjectives that behave like nouns
steps.point: The negative じゃない ends in ない again, so it carries on as an い-adjective: じゃなかった, じゃなくて.

steps.title: Potential
steps.subtitle: Being able to do something
steps.point: Every potential is an ordinary ichidan verb: 書[か]ける conjugates like 食[た]べる, so 書[か]けない and 書[か]けた need nothing new.

steps.title: Desire
steps.subtitle: Wanting to do something
steps.point: たい is an い-adjective: 書[か]きたくない, 書[か]きたかった and 書[か]きたくて are 高[たか]い's endings on 書[か]きたい.

steps.title: Conditional (たら)
steps.subtitle: If and when
steps.point: たら is the past with ら added, whatever the word: 書[か]いたら, 高[たか]かったら, and for a negative, なかった → なかったら.

steps.title: Provisional (ば)
steps.subtitle: The other conditional
steps.point: An い-adjective replaces its い with ければ: 高[たか]い → 高[たか]ければ. ない is one, so a negative becomes なければ: 書[か]かない → 書[か]かなければ.

steps.title: Passive
steps.subtitle: Having something done to you
steps.point: Every passive is an ordinary ichidan verb, so it takes every form you know: 書[か]かれない, 書[か]かれた.

steps.title: Causative
steps.subtitle: Making or letting someone act
steps.point: Every causative is an ordinary ichidan verb too — so it has a passive of its own: 書[か]かせる → 書[か]かせられる.
